tasks.title: KaneEnabler: fix the Background-pairing eligibility bug in deck-validation

setup.note: build @mtg/rules so the server's (scoped) typecheck can resolve it; cp is a bash-ism so replicate the cp step with Copy-Item

typecheck.note: scope typecheck to the touched module graph only - the full server tsconfig includes scripts/* that need 2 more workspace packages built

tasks.prompt: You are working in the KaneEnabler repository: a Commander (EDH) deck recommender. The deck-validity endpoint calls validateDeck in apps/commander-recommender/server/src/services/deckValidation.ts. There is a bug in commander-unit eligibility: it uses commanders.every((c) => c.is_commander_eligible === 1), but a Background card (the choose-a-background mechanic, CR 702.124) is definitionally is_commander_eligible = 0, so a fully legal commander pair of a chooser plus its Background is rejected with isValid false. Implement the fix and update the matching unit test in deckValidation.test.ts. Requirements: (1) A Background card must be usable as part of a legal commander unit, so a legal chooser+Background pair now validates with commander.pairingLegal true and isValid true. (2) Keep rejecting: Sol Ring named as commander, and two unrelated legends without a pairing ability. (3) The existing unit test "a Background companion needs the legal Background to pair" currently passes only the chooser and never walks the pairing branch. Change it so the Background is actually passed (in the submitted deck AND in the commanders argument) and the assertions cover the pairing branch. (4) The modified test must FAIL if only your eligibility change is reverted while the test stays - it must genuinely depend on the eligibility fix. Change ONLY these two files: apps/commander-recommender/server/src/services/deckValidation.ts and apps/commander-recommender/server/src/services/deckValidation.test.ts. Do not commit. Do not touch any other file. When done, run the server package's deck-validation unit tests and make sure they pass.

tasks.title: lfc-bot: guard fulfill/delete from re-acting on a non-active listing
tasks.source: Identified via codebase survey (2026-09-20), independently verified by reading src/services/listings.ts, its three call sites (src/commands/user/fulfill.ts, src/commands/user/delete.ts, src/commands/admin/remove.ts), the schema (status: active/fulfilled/deleted/expired, see src/services/listing-expiry.ts), and existing test coverage (tests/services/listings.test.ts, tests/commands/user/fulfill.test.ts, tests/commands/user/delete.test.ts - all only ever seed status:'active'). Deliberately a missing-validation bug, not another eligibility/conditional-logic bug like kane-01.

typecheck.note: tsconfig.json excludes tests/ (confirmed empirically - an explicit include of the test file is still dropped by the inherited exclude), so this extends tsconfig.eslint.json instead, which already overrides exclude to admit tests/ - confirmed via `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` that both files are actually type-checked under it, not silently skipped.

tasks.prompt: You are working in the lfc-bot repository: a Discord bot for trading Magic: The Gathering cards. Listings are marked terminal via two service functions in src/services/listings.ts: fulfillListing(id) and softDeleteListing(id), both implemented through a shared setStatus(id, status) helper. There is a bug: setStatus updates the listing's status by id alone, with no check on the listing's CURRENT status - it runs db.update(listings).set({ status, updatedAt: now() }).where(eq(listings.id, id)).run(). This means a listing that is already 'fulfilled', 'deleted', or 'expired' can be fulfilled or deleted again, silently resurrecting it. The command handlers (fulfill.ts, delete.ts, admin/remove.ts) only check listing ownership or server membership, never the listing's current status, so this reaches production behavior directly. Implement the fix and update the matching test coverage in tests/services/listings.test.ts. Requirements: (1) setStatus (and therefore fulfillListing and softDeleteListing) must only change a listing's status when its CURRENT status is 'active' - calling fulfillListing or softDeleteListing on a listing whose status is already 'fulfilled', 'deleted', or 'expired' must leave its status unchanged. (2) Calling fulfillListing or softDeleteListing on a genuinely active listing must still work exactly as before. (3) Add test coverage in tests/services/listings.test.ts proving this: seed a listing, call softDeleteListing on it once, then call fulfillListing on the same id and assert its status is still 'deleted', not 'fulfilled' (and the symmetric fulfill-then-delete case). (4) Your new test must FAIL if only your setStatus fix is reverted while the test stays - it must genuinely depend on the fix, not pass regardless. Change ONLY these two files: src/services/listings.ts and tests/services/listings.test.ts. Do not commit. Do not touch any other file, including the command handlers. When done, run `npx vitest run tests/services/listings.test.ts` and make sure it passes.
